mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen steadily for three consecutive weeks (-9.7 to -8.4), indicating a gradual return of commuting and work-adjacent errands. This continued recovery mechanically lifts weekday retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -9.7 to -8.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is flat or lower than the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, falsifying the commuting-driven footfall link.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen each week (6.6 to 3.7), showing people spending progressively less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL drops below a 4.0-point threshold, reduced home-bound behavior translates into increased discretionary outings, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.0 points in the weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 6.6 to 3.7 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of RESIDENTIAL crossing below 4.0, or RETAIL_REC falls while RESIDENTIAL continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is highly volatile (-15.3, -17.1, -27.3, -16.9), likely reflecting intermittent weather disruptions in early spring. A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS of more than 10 points signals a weather-driven shift of outdoor activity indoors, boosting retail and recreation visits the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -17.1 to -27.3 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: Following a PARKS drop exceeding 10 points, RETAIL_REC does not rise in the subsequent week, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise together week-on-week, the combined restoration of commuting infrastructure and office attendance has an amplified effect on retail footfall beyond either series alone, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase in the same week relative to the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is no greater than predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint increases in both series.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined steadily (2.3 to 1.3), suggesting reduced precautionary stockpiling typical of a post-restriction normalization phase. As essential-goods behavior normalizes, consumer spending reallocates toward discretionary retail and recreation, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 2.3 to 1.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise as GROCERY_PHARM continues to decline, or RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM move in the same direction, contradicting the reallocation mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September marks the onset of spring in NSW, historically associated with increased outdoor and retail activity as daylight hours lengthen. This seasonal shift supports a gradual four-week rise in RETAIL_REC independent of any single mobility series' short-term fluctuations.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2022-09-15, start of Southern Hemisphere spring
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows no net increase relative to the prior 28 days despite the seasonal spring transition.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed (around -27 to -31), indicating that commuting infrastructure use has not meaningfully recovered. As long as TRANSIT stays below -25, constrained public transport capacity will continue to cap retail and recreation visits over the coming week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25 points for the weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has stayed between -27.3 and -31.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week even though TRANSIT remains below -25, indicating transit suppression no longer constrains retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL and rise in WORKPLACES jointly indicate a fuller behavioral return to pre-pandemic routines than either series shows alone, producing a stronger compounding uplift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL decreases and WORKPLACES increases in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell while WORKPLACES rose across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is not greater than the sum of effects predicted from RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES individually, or RETAIL_REC declines despite the joint pattern persisting.
